newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up on Friday on a technical rebound supported by rumours that Beijing would shortly cut bank interest rates, traders said.
The index rose 0.899 points or 1.48 percent to 61.678 points, on volume of 17.1 million shares worth $6.5 million against $9.1 million on Thursday.

Traders said there was some bargain-hunting after Thursday's falls and the rumours pushed some long-term investors to build positions. Institutional support for selected firms including real estate developer Lujiazui and clothes maker Shanghai Kaikai also helped to push up the index, they said.

But market sentiment remained cautious due to concerns about possible specific measures to implement the reaffirmed ban on domestic investors buying B shares could be announced during a national meeting of bankers next week.
"Buying was sporadic with major investors cautious on the concerns," one broker said. "They are worried that (measures to ban domestic investors) will cause the market to fall."
"It will be difficult for the index to rise much due to technical resistance around 62-63 points with market sentiment unstable," a second broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 33 up, four flat and six down.
Industry Sewing Machine was the star on speculative buying, jumping $0.012 or 7.69 percent to $0.168 on volume of 47,000 shares.
Heilongjiang Electric Power followed on a rebound after sharp losses in the previous days, gaining $0.026 or 4.81 percent to $0.566 on volume of 893,900 shares.
Newcomer clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was still the most active stock on institutional support, rising $0.008 or 2.53 percent to $0.324 on volume of 5.9 million shares.
Shanghai's A share market rose in line with B shares on rumours of a possible cut in bank interest rates, but trading remained sluggish on cautious sentiment, brokers said.

The A index ended up 11.871 points or 1.25 percent to 958.913 points on volume of 304.8 million shares worth 2.8 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index gained 19.590 points or 0.81 percent to 2438.240 points.
Xinjiang Tunhe was the biggest winner on news that it had bought shares in a trust and investment firm, soaring 1.23 yuan or limit-up of 10 percent to 13.48 yuan on volume of 2.8 million shares.
